question: A 14-year-old suspect in a criminal matter requires radiographic age estimation to determine whether he was a minor at the time of the alleged offence. He has no documentation of birth. Which reference standard is MOST appropriate?

answers.text: The Greulich and Pyle atlas of the hand and wrist.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The Greulich and Pyle (G&P) hand-wrist atlas is the standard first-line reference for age estimation in adolescents (typically 0–19 years). A left-hand-wrist radiograph is compared with atlas plates to assign a skeletal age. For ages near the 18-year legal threshold, the clavicle medial epiphysis fusion may be added as a supplementary method.

Incorrect. Dental eruption patterns are used when the estimated age is below 14 years or in very young children. In a 14-year-old suspect approaching legal majority, skeletal reference standards (Greulich and Pyle for the hand-wrist) are more reliable for the relevant age range.

answers.text: CT brain scan for degree of cerebral myelination.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. CT brain myelination is not a validated method for medico-legal age estimation in adolescents. Ionising radiation exposure for this purpose would be ethically unjustifiable. The Greulich and Pyle hand-wrist atlas is the appropriate validated standard.

Incorrect. Tanner staging describes pubertal development and is not a standalone radiographic reference standard. Radiographic age estimation in this context requires skeletal standards such as Greulich and Pyle.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the section on reference-standard selection. For an adolescent, the Greulich and Pyle atlas of the hand and wrist is the appropriate validated standard.
Correct. The Greulich and Pyle hand-wrist atlas is the primary reference standard for adolescent radiographic age estimation.
